content.title: Time for the module challenge
content.body:
You've finished the lessons in this module. Now it's time to review the big ideas.

This quiz covers:

• What programming is
• How computers follow instructions
• Why bugs happen
• What algorithms are
• What Python is used for

Take your time. There is no timer, and every question includes an explanation after you answer.

quiz.question: A program is a list of instructions that a computer follows step by step.
quiz.explanation: Correct. Programs are made from instructions that computers follow in order.

quiz.question: In the Input → Processing → Output model, what does processing mean?

options.text: Showing a result on the screen
The computer doing something with the input

quiz.explanation: Processing is when the computer works with the input before producing a result.

quiz.question:
Your robot instructions say:

1. Pour the juice
2. Open the bottle

What happens?

options.text: The robot opens the bottle first because it is smart
The robot pours the juice successfully
The robot tries to pour from a closed bottle

quiz.explanation: Computers follow instructions in the exact order they are given.

quiz.question: What is a bug in a program?

options.text: A program that is too long
A mistake in the code that causes problems
A feature that is hard to use

quiz.explanation: A bug is a mistake in the code that makes the program behave in a way the programmer did not expect.

quiz.question: What is an algorithm?

options.text: A precise, step-by-step plan for solving a problem

quiz.explanation: An algorithm is a clear plan for solving a problem step by step.

quiz.question: Python was named after the snake.
quiz.explanation: Correct. Python was named after Monty Python, a British comedy group.

quiz.question: Which of these is something Python is commonly used for?
quiz.explanation: Python is commonly used for websites, data analysis, automation, AI, science, and many other kinds of software.

quiz.question: You want to build a quiz game, but it feels too complicated. What is the programmer's approach?

options.text: Write all the code at once
Give up because it is too hard
Wait for someone else to build it
Break the problem into smaller steps

quiz.explanation: Programmers solve large problems by breaking them into smaller, manageable pieces.

quiz.question: Why are computers good at repetition?

options.text: They never get bored repeating instructions

quiz.explanation: Computers can repeat instructions quickly and accurately without getting tired or bored.
